name: std::prev

declarations.code:
template <class BidirIt>

BidirIt prev(BidirIt it, typename std::iterator_traits<BidirIt>::difference_type n = 1);

template <class BidirIt>

constexpr

    BidirIt
    prev(BidirIt it, typename std::iterator_traits<BidirIt>::difference_type n = 1);

intro: Return the nth predecessor (or -nth successor if n is negative) of iterator it.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
it

 -

 an iterator


 n

 -

 number of elements it should be descended


 Type requirements


 -BidirIt must meet the requirements of LegacyBidirectionalIterator.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: An iterator of type BidirIt that holds the nth predecessor (or -nth successor if n is negative) of iterator it.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.text:
Linear.

However, if BidirIt additionally meets the requirements of LegacyRandomAccessIterator, complexity is constant.

sections.title: Possible implementation
Notes
sections.text: Although the expression --c.end() often compiles, it is not guaranteed to do so: c.end() is an rvalue expression, and there is no iterator requirement that specifies that decrement of an rvalue is guaranteed to work. In particular, when iterators are implemented as pointers or its operator-- is lvalue-ref-qualified, --c.end() does not compile, while std::prev(c.end()) does.
